expected.charges: McComb's first sit-in at the segregated Woolworth lunch counter, conducted with Curtis Hayes
expected.convicted: No — a later account states the charges were eventually dropped
expected.sentence: 34 days in jail under harsh conditions; he reportedly lost 18 pounds. The exact discharge date has not been located — 34 days from the August 26, 1961 arrest places his release around September 28-29, 1961, entered at approximate precision.

updates.sentence: Reportedly spent 34 days in jail after the Woolworth sit-in, according to the Civil Rights and Restorative Justice Project. The exact discharge date is unverified; the former September 29 date was calculated from a duration rather than documented. Contemporary accounts also report 36 days, so that discrepancy remains unresolved.

expected.charges: Disorderly conduct, obstructing traffic and failure to obey an officer during the December 10, 1961 Albany train-station Freedom Ride
expected.sentence: Released at about 4:30 p.m. on December 11 after 24.5 hours, with later county-jail confinement during the campaign; five days in custody in total.

updates.sentence: Released on bond about 4:30 p.m. December 11, 1961, after approximately 24.5 hours, according to her contemporaneous letter. This first stay was separate from the later December 14 county-jail confinement; a combined five-day estimate is not the duration of this first episode.
